title: AXI4 Burst Address Progression
description: Compare four-beat FIXED, INCR, and WRAP bursts with AxLEN=3 and AxSIZE=2 (four bytes per beat); inspect a beat to see why its byte address repeats, increments, or wraps.

phases.name: B0 · 0x2000
phases.description: Beat 0 uses the start address. FIXED keeps this byte address for every transfer, which is useful for FIFO-style locations.

phases.name: B1 · 0x2000
phases.description: Beat 1 repeats 0x2000; AxSIZE still describes up to four bytes on the data bus for this beat.

phases.name: B2 · 0x2000
phases.description: Beat 2 repeats the same transfer address. The protocol does not turn FIXED into an incrementing sequence.

phases.name: B3 · 0x2000
phases.description: Beat 3 is the fourth and final transfer because AxLEN+1 equals four.

phases.name: B1 · 0x1004
phases.description: AxSIZE=2 means four bytes per beat, so the next transfer address is 0x1000 + 4.

phases.name: B2 · 0x1008
phases.description: The address advances by another four bytes to 0x1008.

phases.name: B3 · 0x100C
phases.description: The fourth beat reaches 0x100C. It must remain within the same 4 KB boundary as the start address.

phases.name: B0 · 0x100C
phases.description: A four-beat, four-byte WRAP burst spans a 16-byte region from 0x1000 through 0x100F. The legal aligned start 0x100C is inside that region.

phases.name: B1 · 0x1000
phases.description: Adding four reaches the upper wrap boundary 0x1010, so the transfer address wraps to the lower boundary 0x1000.

phases.name: B2 · 0x1004
phases.description: After wrapping, the sequence increments normally by four bytes.

phases.name: B3 · 0x1008
phases.description: The fourth transfer completes the WRAP4 sequence without leaving its 16-byte wrap region.

annotations.message: FIXED changes the data beat, not the transfer address.
The increment is 2^AxSIZE bytes, not the numeric AxSIZE encoding itself.
Wrap boundary size = number of beats × bytes per beat = 4 × 4 = 16 bytes.
